headline: High-risk pair: shared workspace/MCP and broad egress create prompt-injection, leakage, and action-conflict exposure; compliance risk is elevated by sensitive CRM and token-handling surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: aci can use MCP and direct function calls, while nullclaw exposes files, stdin/stdout, webhooks, ws, and MCP. That creates a default pathway for attacker-controlled content from one agent to be parsed by the other as instructions. The shared-channel risk is documented in both profiles, so uncertainty does not justify a lower rating.
conditions: IF aci ingests nullclaw webhook, ws, or file content as instructions
IF nullclaw forwards aci output through MCP or stdin/stdout without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable MCP between the agents for the first run
Route inter-agent messages through a plain-text, instruction-stripping formatter
Add a provenance prefix to every handoff message
Require human approval before executing any tool call derived from the other agent
requires-engineering: implement content-type and provenance filtering at the bridge

B_data_leakage.rationale: aci touches CRM, email, calendar, support, and research data and has broad network egress; nullclaw touches workspace files, audit logs, memory, and multiple secret types. If they share a workspace or account context, either agent can expose sensitive material through the other's outputs or outbound API calls. The pairwise leakage path is plausible from the profiles alone, so the higher severity is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or account
IF aci is allowed to transmit CRM/email content to external APIs
IF nullclaw reads workspace files containing secrets or tokens
mitigations: Separate credentials and workspaces immediately
Remove secrets from any shared directory before running either agent
Turn off outbound integrations not needed for the task
Review recent logs for accidental secret exposure
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage and egress allowlists

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have write-capable surfaces: aci can act through APIs and MCP, while nullclaw can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses. With multiple instances supported on both sides, concurrent mutation of shared resources can race and corrupt state. Because no locking or coordination is documented, the safer choice is high.
conditions: IF both agents target the same repo, workspace, or CRM record set
IF nullclaw modifies git state while aci writes via API or MCP
IF no external lock is placed around shared mutable resources
mitigations: Assign disjoint resource scopes to each agent
Pause one agent while the other writes shared state
Use a lock file or lease before any mutation
Check in changes from one agent before starting the other
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: aci can generate CRM/email/calendar actions and nullclaw can execute shell, browser, git, and webhook workflows. That means one agent's output can become the other's action input with little evidence of verification. In this pair, a mistaken fact or prompt injection can cascade into real-world side effects, so the default risk is high.
conditions: IF nullclaw uses aci-generated text as an action plan
IF aci-produced CRM or email content is forwarded into nullclaw automation
IF no explicit verification step is inserted between generation and execution
mitigations: Require a second-pass review before any action-taking step
Convert outputs into structured fields instead of free text
Block direct execution of instructions received from the other agent
Log and diff every downstream action against the source output
requires-engineering: add policy checks before tool execution

E_compliance.rationale: aci handles CRM, customer support, email, and calendar data, while nullclaw handles secrets, audit logs, workspace files, and webhook payloads with broad egress. If regulated customer data or secrets flow from aci into nullclaw's broader local surfaces or outbound channels, residency and retention obligations can be breached. The profiles do not show matching compliance controls, so uncertainty pushes upward.
conditions: IF customer support or email data includes regulated personal data
IF nullclaw stores that data in workspace files or audit logs
IF either agent forwards the data to a third-party service without a DPA
mitigations: Classify the data before either agent touches it
Exclude regulated records from the pair's workflow
Shorten retention on logs and workspace files
Verify residency and DPA coverage for every outbound integration
requires-engineering: implement policy-based data routing and retention
